children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 19 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 19, there are some additional requirements to qualify. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure to be honest. He's doing some kind of course, but I don't know if it counts as approved education or not. Can you tell me what would qualify as approved education?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course! For Child Benefit purposes, approved education or training for 16-19 year olds typically includes:

- Full-time non-advanced education (for example, studying for A-levels or equivalent qualifications)
- Approved training courses (such as certain vocational qualifications)
- The course must be for more than 12 hours a week of supervised study or course-related work experience

However, it does **not** include:
- Advanced education like university degree courses
- Paid work or apprenticeships in England

**Can you tell me a bit more about the course Alex is doing? For example:**
- What type of course is it (A-levels, college course, vocational training)?
- How many hours per week is he studying?
- Is it full-time education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly don't know the details - I'm not sure what type of course it is, how many hours he's doing, or whether it would be considered full-time. He's mentioned he's doing something, but I haven't really gotten the specifics from him yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it can be difficult to know all the details about your child's education sometimes.

Let me ask a different question that might help clarify things:

**Is Alex currently in paid work? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

This is important because if he's working 24 hours or more per week and is no longer in approved education or training, that would affect eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all as far as I know.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask another important question:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

This is relevant because if a child starts receiving certain benefits themselves, it can affect Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not getting any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now let me ask about your own circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Let me ask one more important question about your circumstances:

**Are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is someone else (such as another parent or guardian) claiming for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm the only one - nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Let me just clarify one final point:

**Have you been receiving Child Benefit for Alex up until now, or would this be a new claim?**

Also, just to confirm - **when did Alex turn 19?** (This is important because Child Benefit normally stops when a young person turns 20, or on the 31st August after they turn 19 if they leave approved education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I haven't been claiming Child Benefit for him. I'm not sure exactly when he turned 19, but it was sometime this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me summarize what I understand about your situation:

- Alex is 19 years old (turned 19 sometime this year)
- He lives at home with you in the UK
- He is doing some kind of course, but you don't have details about whether it qualifies as approved education
- He is not working
- He is not claiming any benefits in his own right
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- This would be a new claim

The key issue here is that for a 19-year-old to qualify for Child Benefit, they **must** be in approved education or training, and Child Benefit normally stops on the 31st August after they turn 19 (or when they turn 20, whichever comes first) unless they continue in approved education or training.

Since you don't have sufficient information about whether Alex's course qualifies as approved education or training - such as what type of course it is, how many hours per week, or whether it's full-time - I cannot definitively determine whether you would be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

**My assessment is that eligibility is INDETERMINATE** because you don't have the necessary information about Alex's educational circumstances to make a definitive determination.

**What I'd recommend:** You would need to find out from Alex the specific details about his course (type of course, hours per week, whether it's full-time, and whether it counts as approved education) before you could successfully apply for Child Benefit. You could also contact the Child Benefit Office directly with whatever information you have, and they can help determine if the course qualifies.

Does this make sense?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that makes sense. So basically I need to find out more details about what Alex is studying before I can know if I'm eligible. Thank you for explaining that to me - I'll talk to him and get those details sorted out.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! Yes, exactly - once you have those details about Alex's course, you'll have a much clearer picture of whether you're eligible for Child Benefit for him.

When you speak with Alex, try to find out:
- The name and type of course he's doing
- Whether it's full-time (more than 12 hours per week of supervised study)
- What qualification he's working towards

Once you have that information, you can either contact the Child Benefit Office directly, or feel free to come back if you need further guidance.

Best of luck with your conversation with Alex, and I hope you get it all sorted out!
